questions.q: What are the three stages a company passes before predictable success?
questions.why: Lesson 1 names the early struggle, the fun stage and the whitewater stage that follows them.

questions.q: How much cash does McKeown say a business should keep on hand?
questions.why: Lesson 1 gives the rule of having three times as much cash as you need to stay in business for a year.

questions.q: How should a growing company handle more decisions than it can make?
a: Push them down the chain and let people own them
Centralize them with the founder for consistency
Delay them until the busy period passes
Cut quality or cancel orders to cope
questions.why: Lesson 2 says pushing decisions down frees leaders for strategy and keeps the company moving in hard times.

questions.q: What does the four-D decision system involve?
a: Gathering data, debating, deciding or deferring
Diagnosing, discussing, directing and doubling down
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes the system as data, debate, decide and defer, with a 40 percent rule for gathering data.

questions.q: Which Google practice does McKeown suggest for building risk-taking in?
a: Giving employees a day a week for their own projects
Letting employees vote on the annual budget
Reviewing every new idea in a weekly meeting
questions.why: Lesson 3 cites Google's 20 percent time as an example of making risk-taking part of daily operations.
